newsitem.title: JAPAN: Crudes firm in late Asia, wet trade dull.
newsitem.headline: Crudes firm in late Asia, wet trade dull.

text.p: Crude oil prices firmed in late Asian trade on Thursday, recovering some losses suffered overnight in New York on technical selling, traders said.
January cash Brent was assessed at $22.60/22.70, compared with $22.50/22.55 in late U.S. trading on Wednesday.
In paper spreads, Brent/Dubai for January and February were largely stable with both assessed at $1.95/2.05.

Overnight January Brent/Dubai switched hands at $2.00 and $1.98, while March Brent/Dubai traded at $1.91. Activity in the wet market was slow, with some players sidelined by recent high premiums for Gulf crudes, traders said.
Sentiment in Dubai weakened slightly as a U.S. major was seen offering its cargo. About six January Dubais are said to have been bought by end-users, leaving around 10 cargoes available.
January Dubai was assessed at about full month quotes plus 72 to 75 cents, traders said, adding that end-users seem loathe to buy at above plus 70 cents.
The high premium levels for Dubai may force buyers to turn to Oman, they said. January Oman was last traded at MPM plus 12 cents.
Light grade trading has also lost some momentum.
